327 PM EDT Fri Jul 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Key Messages 1 & 2 were updated.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Warming temperatures into the weekend with mainly hit and miss
  showers or thunderstorms. 

- Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Warming temperatures into the weekend with mainly hit and miss
 showers or thunderstorms.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...

Several shortwave-troughs will traverse the region over the
weekend, while at the surface, light southeasterly flow around
retreating New England surface high will allow for moisture
return into the area. Isolated showers are possible tonight
across southwest areas as low-level moisture returns into
the area. Warming temperatures and increasing instability may
result in isold to sct showers and thunderstorms Sat into Sun,
mainly west of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Moisture and
instability increase further on Monday with greater coverage and
convection spreading east of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...

Ensemble model guidance continues to favor a highly amplified 
pattern across the country next week. Mid/upper heights should 
continue to build across the Desert Southwest into the Great Plains 
region. At the same time, below average heights persist near Hudson 
Bay while extending down along the Eastern Seaboard as an elongated 
trough. This would support a mainly northwesterly flow regime as 
impulses track up and over the sprawling upper ridge across the 
middle of the U.S. These often have a tendency to produce convective 
complexes, some of which result in mesoscale convective systems 
(MCS). Thus, expect some uptick in convective chances during early 
portions of next week.

One more formidable shortwave emerges on Tuesday which will be 
characterized by falling heights/pressures as well as increasing 
moisture advection. This coincides with ample instability rising 
into the 1,500 to 2,500 J/kg range. With enough vertical shear and 
height falls, global models support an active day of thunderstorm 
activity. Ensembles show some sagging of the surface isobaric 
pattern with its position indicative of a lee-side trough. This will 
likely be one focus for convection along with terrain circulations 
and the upstream cold front. Damaging wind gusts and torrential 
downpours are possible with any such storm. Given the later arrival 
of the front, the threat for storms may persist beyond the core 
diurnal heating hours.

Models show this frontal zone sagging southward to near the Virginia-
North Carolina border by mid-week. A shift to post-frontal 
northwesterlies should gradually quell the threat for thunderstorms. 
Dew points begin to fall with temperatures remaining seasonable. 
High temperatures largely top out in the upper 80s to low 90s which 
is close to climatology for late July. Overnight lows fall into the 
60s most nights.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Isolated showers or thunderstoms will be possible west of the 
Blue Ridge Mountains, potentially impacting Charlottesville,
particularly Sat and Sun afternoons. 

The pattern shift will bring a return of convection to the forecast. 
Conditions should stay VFR much of the day on Monday as most 
thunderstorms likely stay back in the higher terrain. However, 
Tuesday is looking like a much more active weather day ahead of a 
notable cold front. Convective-related restrictions become 
increasingly likely, particularly during the afternoon/evening 
hours. Some showers may linger into Wednesday which could be 
accompanied by low ceilings. Gradual improvements take place 
thereafter as winds shift to northwesterly. Before this wind shift 
occurs, expect mainly south to southwesterly winds with afternoon 
gusts to around 15 to 20 knots.

&&

.MARINE...

Light onshore flow 10 kt or less through the weekend. Overall,
great boating weather through the weekend into early next week.

Southerly winds pick up in intensity on Monday evening/night into 
Tuesday. Channeling effects could bring gusts to around 20 knots or 
so, which would be supportive of Small Craft Advisories, 
particularly across wider waters of the Chesapeake Bay. A 
convective threat increases through the day on Tuesday which 
would support the need of some Special Marine Warnings. Winds 
shift to northwesterly by Wednesday with gusts to around 10 to 
15 knots.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...

Tidal anomalies rebound within onshore flow this weekend, with 
more sensitive locations potentially reaching Action Stage 
through the weekend. Annapolis could approach minor flood 
thresholds early next week.
